public_rationale: Read plainly, the claim says many major companies were rushing to add generative AI to their products in early 2023, even though the tools had known safety problems. The record backs this. Google announced Bard on Feb 6, 2023 and said it would bring generative AI into its products, starting with Search. Microsoft launched an AI-powered Bing and Edge on Feb 7. Snap launched its My AI chatbot on Feb 27, and Meta set up a top-level generative AI product group the same day. Reuters described a rush by Big Tech companies to put the technology into their products. On safety, CNBC noted well-documented incidents with Bing's chatbot, and Snap itself warned that My AI 'can be tricked into saying just about anything.' 'Seemingly every major company' is an exaggeration and was not tested literally. But the broad wave he described did happen.
limitations: 'Every major company' is hyperbole and cannot be checked literally; the grade rests on a broad wave among the largest tech firms.
Evidence covers big tech firms; no comprehensive cross-industry count before the post date was found.
Microsoft's primary page shows no date in its text; the date comes from the announcement URL and press coverage.

our_interpretation: 'Seemingly every major company' is rhetorical exaggeration. Plain reading: in the weeks before the post, a broad wave of major (mainly tech) companies publicly announced plans or products to build generative AI into their offerings.
The claim describes the state of affairs when the post was written. Target period is 2023-01-01 to the post date, 2023-03-06.

The trust and safety part is read as: generative AI tools then had publicly known reliability or safety problems (for example misleading or erratic chatbot output) that companies themselves acknowledged.
A literal count showing that every single major company did so is not required, and the claim is not contradicted by a few holdouts.
criteria.support_condition: Several of the largest tech companies (for example Microsoft, Google, Meta, Snap) publicly announced generative AI products or integration plans in early 2023, and there were documented trust and safety problems with these tools at the time.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Few or no major companies announced generative AI integration in early 2023, or the move was limited to one or two isolated firms, or there were no known trust and safety problems with the tools.
